title: The cascade's displacement-step diagram
statement: The figure's circuit runs cylinders $A$ and $B$ through A+ B+ B− A− by the cascade method: group I is A+ B+, group II is B− A−, and the cascade valve CV switches the air between line I and line II. With both cylinders back, S is pressed once. Draw the displacement-step diagram: where each cylinder is at every step line, and which group line is on during each movement.
given: cylinders $A$ and $B$, double-acting, both back at rest
roller valves a0, a1 at $A$'s ends and b0, b1 at $B$'s
the sequence A+ B+ B− A−, in two groups

artefact.caption: Each cylinder at every step line (1 out, 0 back); each group line during the movement after it (1 on, 0 off)

steps.title: Read the circuit
steps.note: Group I is A+ B+ and group II is B− A−. At rest line II is on, and a0, with $A$ back, arms S.

steps.title: Step 1: S pressed
steps.note: S passes line II through a0 to CV's pilot at port 14, so CV shifts: line I comes on and line II goes off. Line I pilots VA straight to its 14 side, so $A$ extends.

steps.title: Step 2: a1 made
steps.note: $A$ out makes a1, which is fed from line I, so VB goes to its 14 side and $B$ extends.

steps.title: Step 3: the group change
steps.note: $B$ out makes b1, so CV switches to line II. Line II pilots VB to its 12 side, so $B$ retracts.

steps.title: Step 4: b0 made
steps.note: $B$ back makes b0, which is fed from line II, so VA goes to its 12 side and $A$ retracts.

steps.title: Step 5: back at rest
steps.note: $A$ back makes a0 again, with S let go: nothing pilots CV, and the cycle stops at rest.

answer: Group I is A+ B+ and group II is B− A−: $A$ is out from step $2$ to step $4$ and $B$ only at step $3$; line I is on for the first two movements, line II for the last two.

stated: cylinders $A$ and $B$, roller valves a0, a1, b0, b1
the sequence A+ B+ B− A−
